summary: Togo Mountain lookout, Colville NF, Ferry County WA: pole tower built 1933 by a CCC-era camp crew; removed or destroyed 1952; footing noted in 2009.

facts.design: 60-foot pole tower with a 7 x 7 ft cab and a ground cabin for living quarters (register and Willhite); a 1933 newspaper says about 70 feet
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin removed or destroyed in 1952; one footing documented in 2009
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Colville National Forest

visit.trail_note: No tower remains. Willhite describes forest-road driving directions to the summit area; that account may be out of date.

events.note: Built by twelve men of the Midget Creek Emergency Conservation Camp, F-6, under Tux Salisbury; completed by late September 1933

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's coordinates (N 48° 56.972' W 118° 23.862') match this record's point. The other coordinate set in the conflict list is not explained by the sources we read.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on height: the register and Willhite say 60 ft, the 1933 Republic News-Miner says about 70 ft, and the record's height_m 21.3 follows the newspaper. The story gives both and does not settle it. Sources disagree on how the tower ended: the register says removed, firelookout.com says destroyed, and Willhite says removed or destroyed; all give 1952. The record's built year of 1933 is supported. The Willhite page header reads 'Togo Mountain Lookout 1939' while its text says 1933; the header was not explained. The record's coordinates differ from west_us_lookouts (48.93434, -118.36724); the register's coordinates match the record, and the other set was not checked. No current source on condition or public access was found. Willhite's photos ('Lookout footings', 'Lookout used for firewood...') have no credit or licence, so none are proposed. The 2009 PDF is a compilation of chapter reports; the Togo entry sits in the Eastern Washington section.
